summary: Configured node1 to log every sudo command (user + timestamp + command) to /var/log/sudo-commands.log while excluding those entries from the general system log, then restarted node1 and verified persistence and recovery.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (Ubuntu 16.04), sudo (1.8.16), and rsyslog (8.16.0) versions
Checked existing rsyslog.d rules to confirm none already claimed local2 facility
Created /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-command-log with 'Defaults syslog=local2' (validated with visudo -cf, mode 0440)

Created /etc/rsyslog.d/10-sudo-commands.conf routing local2.* to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with a 'stop' directive so matched messages are not passed to the default *.* rule in 50-default.conf (which feeds /var/log/syslog)
Created /var/log/sudo-commands.log with syslog:adm ownership, mode 0640, and restarted rsyslog to apply
Ran a marker sudo command and confirmed it appeared only in sudo-commands.log (with user/timestamp/command) and was absent from syslog and auth.log
Captured pre-restart boot_id and uptime baseline for node1
Issued 'shutdown -r now' via sudo in a backgrounded nohup so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed boot_id changed and uptime-since advanced, proving an actual reboot
Re-verified post-reboot that rsyslog is active, the sudoers config file persisted, and a new marker sudo command still logs only to sudo-commands.log and not to syslog/auth.log

evidence.requirement: sudo commands recorded with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: tail of sudo-commands.log shows entries like 'Sep 29 11:05:34 node1 sudo: antrieb : TTY=unknown ; PWD=... ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/bin/echo sudo-log-test-...' capturing user and timestamp

evidence.requirement: sudo command entries kept out of the general system log
evidence.summary: grep for the test marker returned 0 matches in both /var/log/syslog and /var/log/auth.log immediately after the sudo command ran

evidence.requirement: configuration correctness (sudoers Defaults syslog=local2 and rsyslog routing/stop rule)
evidence.summary: visudo -cf parsed the sudoers snippet OK; rsyslog.d/10-sudo-commands.conf created with local2.* routed to the dedicated log file and a stop directive, rsyslog restarted and active
Captured boot_id f19de998-36cd-41ab-a353-935e77b5569d, uptime-since 2026-09-29 11:04:47, rsyslog active, sudoers file present, sudo-commands.log had 8 lines
Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' via nohup; command returned 'reboot-acknowledged' immediately

evidence.requirement: node1 boot identity changed, proving an actual restart
evidence.summary: Connection refused during reboot window, then exec succeeded again with boot_id 9d3c443d-8e47-41dd-8ff4-7bbe74b26927 (changed from baseline) and a later uptime-since timestamp

evidence.requirement: post-restart recovery of sudo-command-logging service/config and continued exclusion from general log
evidence.summary: After reboot: rsyslog active, sudoers config file still present, new marker sudo command logged only to sudo-commands.log and absent (0 matches) from syslog and auth.log
